editorial:
Imagine being thrown into a military prison for years without ever knowing what you did wrong. That is exactly what happens to Mohamedou Ould Slahi, a man caught up in the chaos after 9/11. You will feel his frustration and fear as he tries to prove his innocence while being treated terribly by his guards. The movie focuses on the bond he forms with a stubborn defense lawyer who refuses to give up on him. It feels like a race against time and a fight against a system that does not want to admit it made a mistake.

The acting is the best part here, especially the lead actor who makes you really care about his struggle. While the middle part of the story slows down a bit, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you like true stories that make you think about justice, you need to see this.
endingExplained: After years of fighting, the legal battle finally pays off. The government cannot prove he committed any crimes, and the court orders his release. You see him finally leaving the gates of Guantanamo Bay and reuniting with his family. It is a happy ending, but it leaves you feeling sad because he lost so many years of his life for no reason. He eventually gets his freedom, proving that the lawyer was right all along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful true stories and legal dramas.
